q: What are the emissions of producing acetic acid per tonne?
title: Acetic acid CO2 per tonne
short: Most acetic acid is made by reacting methanol with carbon monoxide. Your Scope 1 and 2 are steam, fuel and electricity for reaction and purification; the methanol and CO bought in, or the syngas you make for them, carry most of the footprint.
audience: Acetic acid producers and buyers in pharma, PTA and textiles

ul: Scope 1: boiler fuel; any CO made on site from gas or coal.
Scope 2: electricity for compressors and pumps.

p: Acetic acid is not a CBAM good. Methanol is not either; hydrogen is, so a plant making its own hydrogen should check.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
